validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DIAMETER — CONFIRMED at high tier, 2 independent sources. Test applied to the sheet's own cited source (egyptoil-gas.com EGAS Annual Report 2018): full-text search of 'Ameriya'/'Dahshour' in pdftotext output returns nothing (as expected per scope guidance — most of NA's 40 rows were ID'd visually off the map, not the text), so I rendered the actual GASCO National Gas Grid map (PDF page 19 of 36 = printed page '35', confirmed by footer numeral) at 200dpi and read it directly. The map shows a distinct, individually-labeled '32"-200 km' green (existing pipeline) line originating at a compressor-station icon immediately beside the W.D.G. Complex / Nobaria P.S. cluster west of Alexandria, running southeast through El Sadat, and terminating at a matching compressor-station icon labeled 'Dahshour' -- i.e. exactly the row's endpoints and both the length (200) and diameter (32) GEM recorded. Second, INDEPENDENT source: GASREG's 'Final Approved TNC April 2020' (Gas Regulatory Authority Transmission Network Code, a different publisher, 2 years later) -- full-text search (pdftotext -layout) hits directly, Section 4.2.4 'DAHSHOUR Compressor Station': "The station receives natural gas via two gas pipelines (El-AMERIA / DAHSHOUR 32" & El-Sadat/DAHSHOUR 42") with inlet pressure range 25:50 Bar ... to be delivered via DAHSHOUR/ELWASTAA 36" and DAHSHOUR/KORIMAT 36" PL then to KORIMAT/BANI-SWIEF 30" ... to feed all south valley consumers." This independently confirms the pipeline's existence, its exact name form ('El-Ameria/Dahshour'), its diameter (32"), its role as an operating transmission trunk into a real, currently-described compressor station (not a gathering/process line -- PipelineType=transmission is correct), and by extension its Fuel=Gas. STATUS: the existing ref-check on 'Status [ref]' flagged the literal word 'operating' as absent from the EGAS PDF -- correctly so, since status here is inferable, not literal (per confidence_tiers.md): both sources describe the compressor station and its feed lines in the present tense as active infrastructure (map's own legend keys this line's line-style as 'EXISTING P/L', not 'UNDER CONS.' or 'UNDER STUDY'), and the TNC (2020) postdates and reaffirms the same live feed described in 2018. Status=operating stands, tier high on context, not a literal-substring miss. DUPLICATE CHECK (watchlist item): distinguished from P8031 'Ameriya Cement-Borg El Arab'. On the same map, 'Ameriya Cement' is a SEPARATE labeled node south of Borg Elarab, connected to it by its own '12"-14km' line -- matching P8031's spec (14 km / 12in) exactly and confirming P8031 anchors on the cement-plant node. P8032's 200km/32in trunk instead originates at the compressor-station icon GASREG's TNC calls 'El-Ameria' (a GASCO transmission-network station, not the cement plant), sitting immediately adjacent to W.D.G. Complex on the map. This matches the previously-established fact that Alexandria-area GEM rows straddle two distinct 'Ameriya' nodes ~10.2 km apart: P8031 uses the cement-plant node, P8032 uses the GASCO station node. Not a duplicate of P8031, P8075, or any other roster row -- each uses a geometrically and functionally distinct anchor point with its own map-labeled length. ATTRIBUTION: StartState/Province=Alexandria and EndState/Province=Giza both check out -- El-Ameria/WDGC sits west of Alexandria and Dahshour (site of the compressor station and the Bent/Red Pyramids) is administratively part of Giza Governorate, not a separate province. SPEC CAVEAT (why 'confirmed (caveat)' rather than a clean 'confirmed'): Diameter (32in) is corroborated by BOTH sources; Length (200km) is stated only on the EGAS map -- the GASREG TNC gives no pipeline-length figures anywhere in the document. No source contradicts 200km, so this is a single-source figure on a lesser field (per the 2+ corroboration standard: medium tier for Length specifically), not a material disagreement, and not grounds for a concern.

summary: P8032 confirmed real (2 independent sources -- EGAS 2018 national-grid map + GASREG TNC 2020, both naming an 'El-Ameria/Dahshour 32"' line feeding the Dahshour compressor station); classification, diameter, status, and both endpoints check out; distinguished by node from P8031's 'Ameriya Cement' anchor, no duplicate. Verdict: confirmed (caveat) -- caveat is that Length=200km rests on the map alone (medium), no fills staged, nothing UNRESOLVED.
